title: Running/Jogging In Place: Benefits, Cautions, and More
content:
Running and jogging are great ways to burn calories. But many people wonder: is jogging in place as effective as running outdoors?

Jogging in place is often used as a warm-up exercise, but it also has its own health benefits. It works different muscles than outdoor running and helps strengthen your ankles and lower legs. If you can’t go outside or don’t have a treadmill, jogging in place can still help you lose weight.

Can Jogging in Place Help You Lose Weight?

Yes! Jogging in place is a good cardio workout. It increases your lung capacity, strengthens your heart and burns calories. The University of Connecticut Health Center even classifies it as a high-energy activity, similar to jumping jacks and jump rope.

How Many Calories Can You Burn?

Your results depend on your intensity. If you jog with effort, a person weighing around 70 kg can burn about 563 calories per hour. Higher intensity = more calorie burn.

The Right Way to Jog in Place

  • Stand straight with feet shoulder-width apart.
  • Look forward and keep your spine neutral.
  • Lift one knee up to hip level and land on the balls of your feet.
  • Alternate legs continuously for 5–10 minutes.

Precautions

  • Do warm-ups before starting and cool down afterward.
  • Stretch your hamstrings, calves, hips and thighs.
  • Start slow and gradually increase speed.
  • Move your arms while jogging to burn more calories.

Excess belly fat increases the risk of health problems like heart disease and diabetes. Cardio workouts such as jogging in place can help reduce belly fat. Always check with your doctor before starting any new exercise routine.

Recommendations

The CDC suggests at least 150 minutes of moderate activity per week. But to lose belly fat, you may need closer to 300 minutes weekly. Studies show people who jog the equivalent of 20 miles per week lose more fat than those who jog less.

Calories Burned Per Hour

On average, jogging in place burns 400–600 calories per hour. Your burn rate depends on:

  • Your body weight
  • Your speed
  • How consistently you move without stopping

Routine Tips

If 30-minute sessions feel difficult, do 10-minute sessions a few times a day — before work, during lunch or at night. Jogging in place offers this flexibility because it doesn’t require space or equipment.

Diet Matters Too

The best results happen when exercise is combined with a low-calorie, nutritious diet. Focus on:

  • Fruits and vegetables
  • Whole grains and complex carbs
  • Lean proteins
  • Low-fat dairy

These foods help create a calorie deficit while keeping you full and fueling your workouts.

title: Ingredients of Self Motivation
content:
The biggest cause of procrastination is lack of motivation.

We know we need to study, finish assignments or complete tasks — yet we delay them. As a mentor, I see that low self-motivation is one of the biggest barriers students and professionals face.

Motivation is not created by one factor alone. Charles Handy describes three elements that must exist for motivation to work:

  • We must know our needs — security, money, approval, companionship or purpose.
  • We must know what activity will fulfil those needs.
  • We must have the energy or resources — time, money or ability — to complete that activity.

These three factors work together. If even one is missing, motivation will fail.

For example:

  • If we don’t know our needs, nothing will motivate us.
  • If we lack the energy or resources, we cannot finish the task.
  • If we don’t know which activity meets our need, we won’t act.

So we need to link unpleasant tasks to meaningful needs — like connecting an assignment to passing a subject or earning approval.

The same applies when motivating others — if you know their needs and give them the tools to complete an activity, they will be motivated.

Remove any of the three — need, action or resources — and motivation disappears.

How to Build Motivation

1. Weakness is your opponent

Think of motivation like competing against your weaknesses. Laziness, stress and procrastination try to distract you — don’t let them win. Stay alert, act early and don’t lose momentum, while still respecting your limits.

2. Play reward games with yourself

The promise of a reward can work wonders. When a big task feels heavy, attach a small reward to completing it — a treat, a break, something enjoyable. This makes action faster and more exciting.

3. Break big tasks into smaller ones

Overwhelming projects kill motivation. Instead:

  • Divide work into smaller tasks
  • Track your progress
  • Take small breaks to reset
  • Rest, breathe and refuel — even a snack can lift your mood

4. Focus on success, not failure

Remember your achievements — big or small. Each success fuels more positive energy and confidence. Use past wins to power your discipline and keep going.

5. Keep smiling

Start your day with simple positivity — a glass of water, a mirror smile and gratitude. Smiling lifts confidence, improves mood and prepares you to share positivity with others.

Laughing and smiling make life feel lighter — and there is no better fuel for motivation than joy.

title: Capture the Positive Momentum
content:
Finish the Year Strong

If you are meeting your goals, great job! If not, it is never too late to improve. Here are seven simple steps to end the year on a positive note.

1. Set Goals

  • Write down your goals.
  • Make a plan so you do not drift without direction.
  • Remove time-wasting habits.
  • Take smart risks.
  • Follow your road map to reach your destination.

2. Run Your Own Race

  • Focus on your path, not others.
  • Redefine what success means to you.
  • Be patient — progress takes time.
  • Accept failures as learning moments.
  • Keep moving forward even when it feels slow.

3. Focus on Your Skills and Talents

  • Celebrate what makes you unique.
  • Learn from others, but be yourself.
  • Discover your natural strengths.
  • Grow your abilities and work on your weaknesses.
  • Keep learning — emotionally, mentally, socially, and physically.

4. Be Positive

  • Stop doubting yourself.
  • Replace negative thoughts with positive ones.
  • Smile and stay hopeful.
  • Expect challenges but do not quit.
  • Take small steps forward — they still count.

5. Form Strategic Partnerships

  • Work with others as a team.
  • Find a mentor or coach.
  • Learn from people who are ahead of you.
  • Connect with people whose skills complement yours.
  • Surround yourself with supportive leaders.

6. Work Hard

  • Train and prepare — there are no shortcuts.
  • Be willing to sacrifice for your goals.
  • Be persistent and stop procrastinating.
  • Take action — action creates results.
  • Do at least two tasks weekly that move you forward.

7. Enjoy the Journey

  • Life is a long race, not a sprint.
  • Take breaks and recharge.
  • Spend time with people who matter.
  • Celebrate small wins.
  • Help others — true success includes kindness and service.

title: Assertiveness The Right Way of Being!
content:
Assertiveness

Assertiveness means sharing your thoughts, opinions, and needs in a clear and respectful way. It lets you express yourself without hurting others. Being assertive is not selfish. You protect your rights while also caring about the rights of others.

Assertiveness vs Other Behaviors

There are three common ways people respond:

  • Submissive: I lose – You win
  • Aggressive: I win – You lose
  • Assertive: I win – You win

When you communicate assertively, you are more likely to reach your goal without conflict. This creates a win-win situation.

What Stops People from Being Assertive?

Many people want to be assertive but struggle because of:

  1. Fear of change
  2. Not admitting their submissive behavior
  3. Fear of harming relationships
  4. Lack of confidence

Before You Start Becoming Assertive

It helps to first:

  1. Manage the anxiety that comes with change
  2. Understand your values and resolve internal conflicts
  3. Think about possible outcomes of being assertive
  4. Prepare others for the changes they may see in you

How to Develop Assertiveness

You can begin with simple steps:

  • Use “I” messages (example: “I feel…”)
  • Choose clear and respectful words
  • Reflect on your actions and behaviors
  • Create a small action plan to practice assertiveness

Benefits of Being Assertive

The rewards of becoming assertive are powerful:

  • Better relationships
  • A more balanced lifestyle
  • Higher productivity and effectiveness
  • More control over your schedule
  • Reduced stress

Start the journey today — assertiveness leads to growth, peace, and success.

title: Knowing What We Want
content:
Knowing What You Really Want

Many people move through life without a clear goal. Sometimes we know what we want, but we cannot see the path. When we finally understand our desires, we must ask: Is this goal realistic? Will it make life better, or only create frustration?

Everyone wants happiness, but we define it differently. Some see happiness as fun, others see it as fulfillment. Society also shapes how we think about happiness because we compare ourselves to others.

Before chasing a goal, ask yourself:

  • Is this really what I want?
  • Will it bring the happiness I hope for?
  • Will achieving it make my life better?

We have limited time, strength, and resources. Balancing responsibilities and goals is one of life’s biggest challenges. Some choices also have no return, so we must choose wisely. Still, we should stay open to possibilities and never accept defeat.

The Creative Journey

Every creative journey starts with inspiration and continues through hard work. At first, excitement motivates us. But stress, fear, or burnout can take over — especially when writing or creating something meaningful.

Writing can be exhausting. It takes time, energy, and emotion. It can feel risky because there might be no reward. We battle self-doubt, comparison, and fear of failure. Sometimes we stare at the blinking cursor and wonder if we can do it.

To avoid falling into self-sabotage, remind yourself of:

  • What you want
  • Why you started
  • What you have already achieved

Asking Yourself the Hard Question

When someone asks, “What do you really want?”, the answer can feel difficult. Often the first reply is, “I don’t know,” but the deeper meaning might be, “I don’t know what I deserve.”

Life challenges can make goals feel distant. Sometimes it takes loss, change, or crisis to push us to rethink our desires.

Questions that can guide your clarity:

  • Do I want deeper connection?
  • Do I want stronger relationships?
  • Do I want satisfaction in my work?
  • Do I want more self-confidence?
  • Do I want better health or balance?

Growing as a person can feel overwhelming. Anxiety, fear, or pressure may lead us toward escapes instead of growth. We avoid facing our internal struggles because they feel uncomfortable.

The Cycle of Creative Life

The same sensitivity that causes pain can also fuel creativity. Most people start adulthood with dreams and identity, but life’s challenges shake these ideas. It is easy to feel like everyone else has their life together while we struggle.

We compare ourselves with people online, in media, or in our social circles. These comparisons create dissatisfaction, anxiety, or self-doubt. Society tells us to work harder and chase success, but this often deepens stress.

Some people lose motivation when the work becomes difficult. Plans fail, distractions increase, and self-doubt grows. As a result, many give up before they even begin.

A Silver Lining

There is hope. When doubt rises, take care of your body and let go of perfection. Feel your emotions honestly instead of hiding them.

Return to your own desires. Decide what you want, even if it feels small or impossible. No one truly has everything figured out — the people who seem perfect are also fighting their own battles.

Knowing what you want and expressing it clearly can re-ignite your inspiration. Creativity helps us connect with others because humans naturally seek meaning, love, and belonging.

title: Reasons Why Theory Is As Important As Practice
content:
Why Theory Matters

Many people think theory is useless. This article explains why theoretical learning is valuable.

The Common Belief

Many MBA students feel theory is a waste of time. We want results, not explanations — like wanting the fish without learning how to catch it.

When someone gives us theory instead of solutions, we feel frustrated. We want a quick fix to remove the problem.

In theory, after the symptom is gone, we should find the root cause. But in reality, we rarely do this.

A Simple Analogy

Who would you go to when you are sick?

  1. A trained doctor?
  2. A nurse?
  3. A person with similar past symptoms?

The logical answer is the doctor. Others have limited exposure and cannot diagnose correctly. Yet emotionally, we often go to others first before visiting a doctor.

Corporate Parallel

In organizations, people rely on old experience to solve problems. Sometimes companies hire consultants because they understand theory better and look at problems with fresh eyes.

What Makes a Good Doctor?

  1. He learns theories and analysis methods.
  2. He knows how to apply theory creatively.
  3. He has experience using it in real cases.

A quack only has point 3 — limited experience and shallow knowledge.

So Why Study Theory?

  1. It contains distilled knowledge and viewpoints from others.
  2. It encourages healthy questioning — theory is not absolute truth.
  3. We must evaluate where theory works and where it does not.
  4. Applying theory allows us to learn from our own results.
  5. It builds discipline in organizing knowledge — useful in exams and real life.

Internet knowledge cannot replace mental understanding and structured learning.

Why Students Prefer Practical Work

Students often choose cases or practical experience because:

  1. They do not understand the theory
  2. They cannot apply it
  3. They dislike the book
  4. They dislike the teacher

But cases are only part of the picture. They are examples of theory, not replacements for it.

Theory helps us learn how to think — practical experience simply applies it.

title: Thoughts Behind the Words
content:
Understanding People Beyond Their Words

We talk to people every day. Most of the time we take their words at face value. But it can be more helpful to look beyond what they say and understand what they think.

People usually talk about what matters to them — their values, interests, and worries. When others listen, they react to parts of the story that connect to their own priorities.

Simple Examples

If you say you bought a new shirt:

  • One person may ask about the brand.
  • Another may ask how much it cost.

This shows what each person cares about.

If you invite people to an event:

  • One may ask what to wear.
  • Another may ask who will be attending.

Their questions reveal their concerns and interests.

How Reactions Reveal Values

Imagine telling someone that you ended a relationship:

  • Do they blame your partner?
  • Do they blame you?
  • Do they show empathy and just listen?
  • Do they suggest fixing the relationship?
  • Do they tell you to move on?

Their reaction gives clues about how they think and what they might do if they were in a similar situation.

Listening Beyond Words

We understand people better not only by hearing their words but by noticing the thoughts and values behind them.

Once we learn to listen to both the spoken and unspoken parts of a conversation, understanding others becomes much easier.

title: Dealing With Unhappiness Through Positive Reinforcement
content:
Reframing Unhappiness

Unhappiness can be useful if we learn to see it differently. When we understand that unhappiness pushes us to choose, we stop drowning in self-pity.

Why We Feel Unhappy

We feel unhappy when life does not match our expectations. Our desires are unmet.

  • I believe I did good work, but my boss disagrees.
  • I fail to get into my dream school.

These moments create frustration.

The Usual Thought Pattern

When we are unhappy, our thoughts may go like this:

  • I am right, but others are not agreeing.
  • If they were my friends, they would support me.
  • Since they don’t support me, I should not like them.
  • I want to stop them from achieving what they want.

This mindset feels real in the moment, even if it sounds exaggerated later.

What Happens Next?

Since we cannot control others:

  • We feel powerless.
  • We try to control people or
  • We sink into self-pity.

Self-pity brings more negative thoughts that justify inaction. Eventually, people avoid us. In workplaces, poor behavior may even lead to being removed.

Reframing Unhappiness

Unhappiness means the current situation is not working. Instead of wallowing, it can push us toward action.

A helpful question to ask is:

“Yes, I am unhappy. So what actions can I take to change this?”

Beyond Fight or Flight

Animals react with fight or flight. We have more choices.

Choice 1 — Check the Desire

Is this really a need or just wishful thinking?

  • Example: Wanting a Rolex.
  • Does it prove success or impress others?
  • If the purpose can be met another way, you don’t really need it.

Choice 2 — Win Some, Lose Some

Sometimes agreeing today may benefit you later.

  • Example: Instead of arguing with a client to prove you are right, agree now to build goodwill.

Choice 3 — Create a Realistic Action Plan

Instant change rarely happens. When it does not, we give up.

  • Example: Wanting weight loss overnight.
  • Instead, set small goals — 500 grams a month equals 6 kilos a year.

Our challenge is impatience and desire for instant results.

The Key Insight

We have more than one choice when unhappy. Realizing this prepares us to act instead of sinking into self-pity.

In essence, unhappiness can lead to growth.

title: Why you should listen to nature sounds
content:
How Nature Sounds Help You Relax and Focus

Nature sounds can calm your mind and improve focus. Whether you are working or studying, the sounds of nature help your body relax.

Think of flowing water, birds singing, waves at the beach, or rain falling. These sounds make you feel peaceful. Many students use nature sounds to relieve exam stress and block distractions. It is almost like meditation, but much easier.

How Do They Help?

Researchers at Brighton and Sussex Medical School tested this by letting people listen to five-minute nature clips while measuring brain activity, breathing, heart rate, and attention.

They found that:

  • Nature sounds create outward-directed attention — thinking about the world around you.
  • Artificial sounds create inward-directed attention — thinking about yourself.

When attention turns inward, we overthink and feel stressed. Nature sounds shift attention outward and reduce anxiety. The study also showed heart rate changes, especially in people who were already stressed — meaning they relaxed more.

Benefits of Nature Sounds

1. Better Focus

If you want to block distractions and improve concentration, nature sounds help like pleasant white noise. Many people stop checking their phones because their mind stays engaged with the sound.

2. Relaxation

Nature sounds make you feel like you are outdoors. Within 10–15 minutes, stress and tension reduce. They work when you are tired, anxious, or upset.

3. Improved Sleep

Nature sounds help people fall asleep faster by masking noise and calming the mind. The repetitive sound pattern gently leads you into deeper sleep. Severe sleep issues still require medical help, but for mild problems they work well.

4. No Side Effects

Nature sounds are safe. Just avoid loud volume, and maybe do not listen to running water when you already need to use the bathroom.

5. Not Addictive

You can stop anytime without withdrawal. They do not create dependency like some other focus tools.

My Experience

For me, nature sounds helped with focus at work. Even after silencing my phone, I kept checking messages. Classical music was distracting, but rain sounds worked beautifully.

After listening for a few hours, my concentration improved a lot. Now I rarely feel the urge to check notifications.

The only challenge is finding a track you like. If the first one annoys you, try others — there are many types of nature sounds.

How to Use Nature Sounds

The process is simple:

  • Pick a track you like
  • Adjust the volume
  • Sit or lie down comfortably
  • Listen and imagine the environment around you

Within 10–15 minutes, you should feel calmer.

With your phone and internet, you can access nature sounds anywhere — especially on apps and YouTube.

title: Running For Fat Loss
content:
Jogging and Belly Fat Explained

Jogging is a great exercise for your heart and overall health. It will not burn belly fat alone, but it helps you lose weight across your whole body. Even a 20-minute jog can help if you do it regularly. If you are new to exercise, check with your doctor before you start.

The Truth About Targeted Fat Loss

You cannot choose where your body burns fat. You may lose belly fat early or it may be the last place to shrink. Keep going — if you continue to lose weight, you will eventually lose fat from your stomach and everywhere else.

How Many Calories Do You Need to Burn?

To lose 1 pound (0.45 kg) of fat, you must burn 3,500 more calories than you eat.

  • A 130-lb (59 kg) person must jog about 500 minutes in total.
  • A 160-lb (73 kg) person needs over 400 minutes.
  • A 190-lb (86 kg) person needs about 350 minutes.

What Does a 20-Minute Jog Do?

A short jog will not burn a lot of calories, but it is a strong starting point.

  • At 130 lbs, you burn about 138 calories in 20 minutes — meaning more than 25 jogs to lose 1 pound.
  • At 160 lbs, you burn around 170 calories — more than 20 jogs to lose 1 pound.
  • At 190 lbs, you burn about 201 calories — more than 17 jogs to lose 1 pound.

Why Diet Matters

Running alone does not guarantee belly fat loss. Diet plays a key role.

  • Track your food intake.
  • Create a calorie deficit.
  • Combine exercise and healthy eating.

If you cut calories and jog regularly, you can reduce 500–1,000 calories per day. That can help you lose 1–2 pounds per week in a healthy way.

title: What happens to your body if you suddenly stop training?
content:
What Happens When You Quit Working Out

Staying fit is not easy. It needs effort, patience, and determination. The first few days feel exciting and motivating. But once you start seeing results, many people relax and stop. Quitting your workout routine can have quick negative effects.

1. A Fast Drop in Fitness

Your belly will not grow overnight, but your fitness level will fall. If you stop a cardio routine, your cardiovascular fitness can decline noticeably within the first three weeks.

2. Fitness Declines Over Time

If you had high fitness levels, they may drop after about 12 weeks of quitting. People with low or moderate fitness may hold stamina for a few weeks, but it will still fade gradually.

No matter what routine you followed, you may notice these changes:

3. Belly Fat Returns

Within a week, you may feel your belly becoming bigger. Your metabolism slows down and muscles are no longer burning calories effectively.

4. Blood Pressure Fluctuates

On days you exercise, your blood pressure stays normal. On days you skip workouts, it rises. After about two weeks, your blood vessels adapt to a less active lifestyle.

5. You Get Tired Easily

Without exercise, you lose muscle efficiency. You may gasp for breath even after climbing stairs because your muscles are not converting oxygen into energy.

6. Your Brain Suffers Too

Exercise improves mood and reduces stress. When you stop working out, you may feel tired, irritable, or low.

7. Muscles Shrink

When you quit training, muscles weaken and begin to shrink. It takes much longer to rebuild lost muscle than to lose it.

title: Blaming Others for Your Unhappiness
content:
Why Blaming Others Holds You Back

It is easier to blame someone else when life goes wrong.

You might blame:

  • Your boss for a bad job
  • Your teacher for not understanding lessons
  • Your partner for relationship problems
  • Your parents for emotional struggles
  • The government for poverty or hardship

Blaming others feels good for a moment. It protects us from regret, guilt, and shame. If we blame ourselves, we face our mistakes — and that can feel painful.

But blaming others does not fix anything. It increases bitterness and takes away your power to change your situation. When you blame others, you feel helpless and stuck. You give up control over your own life.

Blaming can act like a defense mechanism. It protects your ego but hides the truth. It blocks growth and stops real change from happening.

A healthier way is to take responsibility for your situation. Doing this opens the door to:

  • Self-awareness
  • Learning from mistakes
  • Personal growth

When you stop blaming others, you gain the power to improve your life.

title: Choose Carefully the People around You
content:
How the People Around Us Shape Who We Become

Many things we do are influenced by how we want others to see us. We often take on roles based on what people expect.

  • A child behaves well to gain love from parents.
  • A friend follows the group to feel accepted.
  • A professional works hard to be seen as successful.

We all want approval and acceptance. Some people even crave attention or praise. Because of this, the people around us strongly influence our identity.

Why Our Circle Matters

We should reflect on who we spend time with, because we naturally try to please the people we value.

Humans are tribal. Once we identify with a group — whether through beliefs, lifestyle, or interests — we usually follow its norms.

  • Outgoing people seek other extroverts.
  • Health-conscious people join fitness groups.
  • Traditional people may choose conservative companions.

How Groups Influence Behavior

The groups we belong to shape how we think and act. We must ask:

  • Who are the important people in my life?
  • How do their expectations influence my behavior?

For example, if a teen joins a group that drinks or engages in risky habits, they may change just to fit in.

This is one reason why gangs are dangerous — people conform to group expectations, even when they are harmful.

When someone finds belonging in a criminal group, it becomes easy to justify wrongdoing. Their identity becomes tied to the group, making it difficult to leave.

Choosing the Right People

To grow, we need clarity about:

  • Who we are
  • The kind of person we want to become
  • The values we want to live by

It is wise to surround ourselves with genuine people who accept our true selves — not just the version that tries to please them.

title: Simple steps to deal with your sleep problems
content:
5 Tips to Help You Fall Asleep

Struggling to sleep is frustrating. It could be due to stress, anxiety, poor habits, or just bad luck. The good news is there are simple things you can try to help yourself fall asleep faster.

1. Listen to Nature Sounds

This may sound unusual, but you don’t need to go outdoors. Nature sounds are calming because your brain reads them as safe and non-threatening. This reduces stress and relaxes your mind.

You can find these sounds on YouTube, apps, websites, or CDs. There are many types — rain, waves, forests, streams — so you can choose what feels soothing.

2. Do Simple Exercises

No one wants to work out when they can’t sleep, but short, moderate exercise can help. It burns excess energy and relaxes your body.

Keep workouts brief. Too much exercise may make you more awake. Another option is to exercise earlier in the day — morning and evening sessions can reduce built-up tension and make it easier to sleep at night.

3. Take a Warm Bath or Shower

A warm bath an hour before bed relaxes muscles and prepares your body for sleep. If you prefer a shower, keep the temperature warm — not too hot and not too cold. Lukewarm water helps you unwind without waking you up.

4. Watch Your Diet

Food and drink habits affect your sleep. Avoid eating close to bedtime, especially sugary snacks like chocolate or sweets.

Stay away from caffeine in the evening — coffee, tea, and fizzy drinks can keep you awake. Instead, try warm milk or herbal tea for a calming effect.

5. Get Up for a Short Time

If you can’t sleep, don’t just toss and turn. Get up and do something simple like reading or light chores.

Avoid screens or video games because they stimulate your brain. After 10–20 minutes, return to bed — you may find you fall asleep much easier.

Sleepless nights happen to everyone, but with these tips, you can improve your chances of drifting off faster next time.

title: Incredible Weight Loss Myths Exposed
content:
Why Running Alone Isn’t the Best Way to Lose Weight

Many people believe running will melt away extra weight. Running is healthy and has many benefits, but relying on it alone for weight loss is not ideal.

Running Has Great Benefits

Running boosts mood, improves sleep, and strengthens your heart. Studies show runners may have a lower risk of heart disease and may even live longer. So if you enjoy running, keep going — it supports overall health.

Why Weight Loss Stalls With Only Running

In the first few weeks, you may lose some weight because your body reacts to new stress. But soon your body adapts, your progress slows, and the scale stops moving.

To improve, you must keep challenging your body — increase speed, distance, or change your routine.

Running Can Mislead You About Calories

Exercise makes you hungry, but hunger does not match calories burned. Many runners:

  • Overestimate how many calories they burn
  • Underestimate how much they eat afterward

This makes weight loss harder.

HIIT Is More Effective for Fat Loss

High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) burns more calories in less time. It involves short bursts of hard effort followed by rest. You can do HIIT with:

  • Strength training
  • Cycling
  • Cardio workouts
  • Running intervals

Example: Sprint past every third street pole, then walk for two poles before sprinting again.

Research shows HIIT can be more effective for fat loss than steady, slow running.

Why HIIT Works Better

  • High effort burns more energy quickly
  • Your body continues burning calories after the workout (afterburn)

To avoid burnout, limit HIIT sessions to 2–3 times per week, and do lighter exercise in between.

Diet Matters Most for Weight Loss

Exercise alone rarely leads to big weight change. Pairing activity with healthy eating produces the best results.

If your goal is weight loss:

  • Create a calorie deficit safely
  • Focus on nutritious foods
  • Seek guidance from a dietitian if possible

A simple approach is the plate method:

  • Half plate: vegetables
  • Quarter plate: whole grains
  • Quarter plate: lean protein

The Best Workout Is One You Enjoy

HIIT is effective, but it isn’t for everyone. The best exercise for weight loss is one you like and can stick to long term.

Exercise should be enjoyable, not a burden. Whether your goal is health, strength, or weight loss — combine movement you like with mindful eating for lasting results.

title: Things You Should Never Do After a Run
content:
Common Post-Run Mistakes to Avoid

A good run feels amazing. It boosts energy, lifts mood, and makes us feel productive. But what you do after your run matters too. Some habits can reduce the benefits of your workout. Here are five mistakes to avoid after running.

1. Not Refuelling or Hydrating

Any workout uses energy and causes fluid loss through sweat. If you do not eat or drink after running, your body cannot recover well.

  • Eat a light, nourishing meal within 20–30 minutes.
  • Drink water to replace lost fluids.
  • Avoid overeating — too much food slows recovery.

2. Becoming a Couch Potato

Rest is important after running, but lying down immediately can slow recovery.

  • Do light movement instead — gentle walking or stretching.
  • Keep blood flowing so your body recovers faster.

3. Staying in Sweaty Clothes

After running, sweat-soaked clothes hold bacteria.

  • This can cause skin problems.
  • Damp clothes can even make you feel cold.
  • Change clothes as soon as possible, even before showering.

4. Doing Heavy Chores

If your day includes physical tasks, wait a bit before doing them.

  • Your muscles are tired and need time to recover.
  • Heavy chores can strain your body and make you more exhausted.

5. Taking a Hot Bath Immediately

A hot bath may feel soothing, but it is not the best first step.

  • Start with something cold — use an ice pack to reduce soreness and swelling.
  • Rest for a while, then enjoy a warm bath if you want.

By avoiding these mistakes, you get more benefits from your run and recover faster.

title: Common Excuses People Make for Not Getting a Workout
content:
Common Workout Excuses and How to Overcome Them

Exercise offers amazing benefits, but staying committed is not always easy. Many people give in to excuses that stop their progress. Here are common excuses people use — and why you shouldn’t let them hold you back.

1. “I didn’t sleep enough.”

Sometimes you may lose sleep to keep your morning workout. Instead of skipping exercise, try going to bed earlier next time. Staying consistent matters more than getting a perfect eight hours every night.

2. “I’m sore from yesterday.”

Soreness means your muscles worked hard and are adapting. Instead of skipping a session, do light stretching or gentle movement to help recovery.

3. “I feel tired.”

Exercise often reduces tiredness by boosting energy and mood. If fatigue continues for many days, talk to a doctor — but don’t avoid your workout just because you feel a little sluggish.

4. “I ate well today, so I don’t need to work out.”

Diet matters, but exercise gives benefits food alone cannot provide — stronger muscles, better mood, improved metabolism, and heart health. Eating right is not a reason to skip movement.

5. “My gym buddy isn’t coming.”

Friends can motivate you, but your fitness journey is yours. Don’t let someone else’s schedule decide your progress. Learn to stay committed even when alone.

6. “I have an important meeting.”

Exercise helps your brain. It releases endorphins and improves focus. Research shows that aerobic workouts may boost memory and learning — so a workout before a big meeting can actually help you perform better.

7. “I just got back from vacation.”

A break often makes people lose momentum. The longer you wait, the harder it becomes to restart. Get back into your routine quickly — your health depends on it.

8. “I can’t wash my hair today.”

Some people avoid workouts because sweaty hair feels inconvenient. Washing hair after every session can dry it out, but there are products and treatments that help keep hair healthy. Talk to your stylist and find solutions instead of skipping workouts.

Remember, excuses slow progress. Stay committed and enjoy the long-lasting rewards of regular exercise.

title: Balancing Rest, Relaxation, and Exercise for Effective Self-Care
content:
Self-Care: Why It Matters and How to Practice It

The modern world is busy and demanding. Still, you can take care of yourself with simple mental and physical habits.

What Is Self-Care?

Self-care means doing things that leave you feeling well and balanced. It includes choices that support your health and happiness.

For example:

  • If exercising in the morning makes you feel good, that is self-care.
  • If cooking a healthy dinner for your family brings you joy, that is also self-care.

Why Self-Care Is Important

Too much stress harms your health. Since most people deal with stress, it is important to include rest, relaxation, mindfulness, and movement in your routine. Self-care reduces stress and improves overall wellbeing.

Self-Care for Fitness Lovers

Exercise is great, but focusing only on workouts and ignoring rest can backfire. Try balancing both.

Here are helpful fitness self-care tips:

  • Practice breathing exercises.
  • Encourage yourself during workouts.
  • Warm up, stay hydrated, and cool down.
  • Avoid checking messages or social media — stay focused.
  • Track your progress or remind yourself of your goals.
  • Listen to your body — stretch well and consider monthly massage.
  • Wear workout clothes that fit well and make you feel confident.

Other Ways to Practice Self-Care

Relaxation is just as important as activity. Make time for guilt-free rest.

  • Create a quiet space to relax or meditate.
  • Establish a calming nighttime routine — warm bath, soft music, tea.
  • Limit screen time and turn off social media.
  • Read a book.
  • Spend time with friends — go for a walk, workout, or share a meal.
  • Meditate for 10–15 minutes to reset your mind.

Improve Your Sleep Quality

Good sleep is a major part of self-care. Try these expert tips:

  • Use a comfortable mattress, pillow, and breathable bedding.
  • Use relaxation techniques before bed — breathing, meditation, or muscle relaxation.
  • Keep your room cool — around 65–72°F (18–22°C).
  • Let fresh air circulate.
  • Avoid screens in bed.
  • Block noise with white noise if needed.
  • Stay hydrated during the day and avoid caffeine or alcohol late at night.

Choose Three Core Self-Care Activities

Pick three meaningful activities you can do often. Choose ones that improve your mood, fit easily into your routine, or can be combined with other habits.

Make a Self-Care Schedule

Plan regular 20-minute blocks for your activities. Try different times until you find what works best.

If you skip an activity, adjust the schedule or change the task so it is easier to stick with. Good self-care routines are flexible.

The Goal of Self-Care

The aim is to:

  • Reduce stress
  • Support wellbeing
  • Improve your work–life balance

There is no single right way — find what works best for you.

title: Challenge the Way We Think
content:
How Thoughts Shape Feelings and Actions

Our actions often come from how we feel in the moment. Whether we are happy, sad, angry, or afraid, our emotions influence our behavior.

But those emotions usually begin with our thoughts. For example, if we see people whispering and one of them looks at us, we might assume they are talking about us. That thought may be true or false — but it creates a feeling.

If we believe they are whispering about us, we may feel anxious or hurt. Our reaction will match the thought and emotion that came first.

How Decision-Making Helps Us Grow

Every decision we make strengthens our ability to think and analyze. Good choices help build confidence and independence in our thinking.

But sometimes we make wrong choices and must face their consequences. These situations can feel heavy or painful.

How to Reduce Faulty Decisions

We should not constantly doubt ourselves — that weakens confidence. Instead, we should challenge the thoughts that lead to our decisions.

Wrong assumptions or misinterpretations can lead to poor choices. Before deciding, we should question:

  • Is this thought true?
  • Am I assuming something without evidence?

In the whispering example, we should not assume people are talking about us — that is paranoia, not fact.

Think About How You Think

We should regularly reflect on our thinking patterns. Experts call this metacognition.

By doing this, we learn:

  • Why we make certain choices
  • Whether our decisions are healthy
  • How to change unhelpful thinking habits

Understanding our thoughts helps us make better decisions and react more wisely in life.

title: Tips for Success in Achieving Your Fitness and Health

Staying Motivated to Work Out

Talk to Yourself

You can be your own best trainer. Encourage yourself daily. Small actions like five extra squats or ten more minutes of jogging can boost confidence.

Set Small Goals

Unrealistic targets make people quit. Adjust your goals if needed. Take small, steady steps and stay consistent.

Pay Attention to Your Body

Watch how you move. Notice which muscles you are working. When you connect your mind and body, you focus better and stick with your routine.

In life, fitness, relationships, and career, we often understand lessons better after the experience. But you don’t always have to learn the hard way — you can learn from others who have been there.

Lessons From Trainers and Athletes

1. Don’t Be Afraid to Build Muscle

Many people think only heavy weights build muscle. That isn’t true.

  • Body weight exercises, resistance bands, and medicine balls also shape lean muscle.
  • Start resistance training three times a week.
  • Have protein — like a shake or boiled egg — within 45 minutes after your workout.
  • Try boot camp classes for guided resistance training.

2. Make a Plan and Stick to It

A plan helps you stay committed. Schedule workouts — meet a friend, exercise during lunch, or set a fixed time each day.

3. Work Out With a Purpose

Exercising just to “get it over with” is not motivating. Think beyond weight loss.

  • Focus on better health, strength, flexibility, or confidence.
  • These goals help you stay committed long term.

4. Increase Fluid Intake

When you sweat more, you need more fluids.

  • Try half coconut water and half plain water for hydration.
  • To estimate your daily water need: Divide your body weight (in pounds) by two. The result is the number of ounces you should drink.
  • Example: A 150-lb person needs about 75 ounces per day.

5. Manage Cravings Smartly

Cravings may mean your body needs nutrients, water, or rest.

  • Drink water before reaching for snacks.
  • If possible, take a short nap — tiredness can feel like hunger.

6. Have Fun

Exercise does not have to be boring.

  • If you love dancing, try Zumba.
  • If you like challenge, join outdoor boot camps.
  • Do activities you enjoy — enjoyment keeps you consistent.

You don’t need to learn every lesson through trial and error. Use these proven tips to stay motivated, avoid common mistakes, and build healthy habits for life.

title: 4 Abilities Will Polish Your Creative Thinking

Imagine you are improving a doctor’s waiting room. Instead of just adding better seats, ask deeper questions. Comedian Jerry Seinfeld humorously observes the waiting room experience. His perspective inspires fresh questions like:

  • How can we make exam rooms more entertaining?

2. Make No Assumptions

To create new solutions, challenge your beliefs. If you were asked to design a new salad dressing, you might think of new flavors.

But what if you broke assumptions like:

  • Salad dressing must be cold
  • It must be liquid
  • It must be poured on lettuce

Once you question these, your mind opens to new ideas — like a microwaveable salad dressing pouch.

3. Generate Many Ideas

Brainstorming fails when ideas are judged too early. Instead, set time to list many ideas without criticism.

Then pick a few and try combining them. Fresh solutions often appear when ideas mix together.

4. Start Critiques With Positives

It is easy to dismiss ideas. It is harder to grow them.

When reviewing an idea:

  • First ask: What is good about it?
  • Then ask: If it succeeded, what would we achieve?
  • Finally ask: What challenges exist and how can we overcome them?

This mindset helps ideas evolve instead of die too soon.

Creative thinking is a skill anyone can learn. Practice these four habits and you will be seen as a valuable problem-solver at work and at home.

title: The Art of Motivating People to Action
content:
The Four Factors Behind Decisions and Motivation

Many of our actions are influenced by four key elements: justification, alternatives, consequences, and ability. Understanding these helps us manage ourselves and others better.

1. Justification

We act because we believe something is right or necessary. We often tell ourselves we were wronged or that our response is unavoidable. Sometimes we justify based on imagined outcomes that may not actually happen.

2. Alternatives

When emotions run high, we may think there is only one option — often an aggressive or reactive one. Limited emotional control makes it hard to see other choices.

3. Consequences

We must consider whether we can handle the results of our actions. Sometimes fear of retaliation or negative outcomes stops us from acting.

4. Ability

Even if we choose an option, we must ask: Do we have the skill, confidence, or tools to execute it? Ideas without ability remain wishful thinking.

Using These Factors in Motivation

When motivating others, justification becomes the desired outcome — avoiding pain or reaching a benefit.

A good manager understands:

  • What the person values and why the task matters to them
  • What alternatives exist to reach the goal

But leadership should go further:

  • Will the action actually lead to the result?
  • What unintended consequences might appear?
  • Does the person have the capability to execute?

Motivation often fails because execution skills are missing.

Example: Motivating a Team

  • Team members contribute only if the result matters to them. Leaders must link team goals to personal needs.
  • People may refuse tasks if they see them as unfair or beneath them.
  • If they do not trust the promised outcome, they will not commit.
  • Finally, they must have the skill to perform the task.

Example: Changing Jobs

  • We justify leaving — bad boss, poor company, or role change.
  • We explore alternatives, often influenced by peer comparison or fantasy.
  • We check whether the new job will bring money, approval, or status.
  • But we often ignore a key question: Do we have the capability to succeed in that role?

Understanding these four elements helps improve decision-making, leadership, and personal growth.

title: This Is Why Men Run Faster Than Women
content:
Why Men Usually Run Faster Than Women

Both men and women enjoy running, but men generally run faster. This difference is not about effort or commitment—biology plays a major role.

1. Hormones Matter

Before puberty, boys and girls are very similar. When adolescence begins, men produce much more testosterone—up to 20 times more than women.

This hormone helps build muscle, strengthen bones, and increase red blood cells. Women produce more estrogen, which leads to a higher body fat percentage. More fat and less muscle affect running speed.

2. Body Size and Structure

Men usually:

  • Have 80% more leg muscle
  • Have larger lungs and hearts
  • Burn oxygen more efficiently

Women are, on average, 13 cm shorter and 16 kg lighter, with 3–6 kg more body fat. These differences make running harder for women but give them strengths in other sports.

3. Hormonal Impact on Muscle and Fat

Up to age 12 or 13, muscle mass is similar. After puberty:

  • Women gain more fat tissue
  • Men gain more lean muscle

Fat typically makes up 20–25% of women’s weight and 15–20% for men. This affects power and movement efficiency.

4. Oxygen and Energy Use

Running requires oxygen. Here, biology again creates differences:

  • Men’s VO2 max (oxygen capacity) averages 45–50 ml/min/kg
  • Women’s VO2 max averages 35–40 ml/min/kg

Women also have:

  • Less hemoglobin for oxygen transport
  • Hearts that are 30% smaller on average

To compensate, women often have a higher maximum heart rate (174 bpm compared to 169 bpm), but they reach it sooner while running at roughly 10% slower speed.

5. What About the 10% Gap?

Studies show performance differences between men and women in running and many sports hover around 10%.

Women’s best records typically match men’s records from past years. When the gap is greater than 10%, women often improve faster over time.

6. Endurance vs Speed

The difference becomes smaller in endurance events.

Research shows women are often more resistant to fatigue during repeated and static exercises. So while men may excel in speed and strength events, women can have an advantage in endurance-based challenges.

7. What About Other Sports?

The good news is speed isn’t everything. Women possess valuable strengths:

  • Lower center of gravity
  • Better balance and body awareness
  • More flexible muscles and tendons

These qualities can give women an edge in sports that rely on balance, agility, and control.

So while men typically run faster due to biology, women shine in many other ways — especially in endurance and skill-based sports.

title: Running for weight loss?
content:
Running for Weight Loss: Things You Should Know

Cardio workouts are great for weight loss, and running is one of the most popular choices. It boosts fat burning and helps you stay fit. But if running is your preferred way to lose weight, here are some important points to remember.

Stretch Before You Run

Never start running without a warm-up. Stretching helps your muscles open up and improves movement. This reduces injury risk. Simple warm-up exercises also help your joints and muscles get ready for action.

Wear Proper Running Shoes

If you run regularly or plan to start, invest in good running shoes. They protect your feet and reduce stress on your legs. A good pair makes your run smoother, safer, and more comfortable.

Avoid Overeating Before a Run

A heavy meal before running is a bad idea. While it may seem like running will help digestion, it actually slows it down. During running, blood flows to your working muscles, not your stomach. This can lead to cramps or discomfort.

Stay Hydrated

Water is essential for weight loss and running performance. Drink enough water throughout the day to stay energized and prevent dehydration. Avoid sugary or caffeinated drinks before and after your run.

Be Consistent

Running for just a day or two will not give results. Consistency matters most. Stick to your routine, build endurance gradually, and you will see progress over time.

title: How To Have Better Control Over Habits
content:
How to Change Habits and Leave Your Comfort Zone

When we change a habit, it is like creating a new path through a jungle. This can be hard, but it is possible when we understand how habits work.

Why We Feel the Need to Change

When we start thinking about doing an MBA or entering corporate life, we often notice gaps in our skills.

  • We procrastinate.
  • We react too emotionally.
  • We struggle to manage relationships.

This makes us realise that we must change.

At first, we feel excited and full of energy. But after some time, our motivation drops and we slide back into old habits. Then we justify our inaction.

What Is a Comfort Zone?

A comfort zone is a mental space where our habits feel easy and safe.

  • When we repeat a habit, our brain creates a strong neuron path.
  • The habit moves from conscious effort to automatic behaviour.
  • This path becomes smooth, familiar, and easy to follow.

Because this old path is easy, we naturally keep using it.

Changing a Habit Is Like Making a New Path

When we change a habit, we create a new path in our brain.

  • It feels like cutting through a jungle.
  • We must push through resistance from ourselves and others.
  • We must repeat the new habit many times to make the new path smooth.

This is difficult. So many people give up and go back to the old path.

Even when the new path exists, we still have two choices:

  • The new, uncomfortable path.
  • The old, easy one.

Most of the time, we choose the old one.

How to Handle This and Change Better

1. Choose the Right Path Early

  • Think before you start a habit.
  • The first time is hard, but it gets easier each time.
  • Bad habits like bribery or cheating also begin with one “small” step.

2. Understand the Benefits of the New Habit

  • Know clearly why you want the change.
  • List the benefits of the new habit.
  • Use these benefits to stay motivated.
  • Walk on the new path many times until it feels normal.

3. Close the Old Path

  • Remove temptations that pull you back.
  • Make it hard to return to the old habit.
  • Change your environment if needed.

Example: Breaking an Addiction

  • Step 1: Decide not to smoke (or any habit you want to stop).
  • Step 2: Find a stronger emotion than the desire to smoke, such as love for your family or concern for your health.
  • Step 3: Get support:
    • Ask friends and family to stop you from smoking.
    • Reward yourself for smoke-free days.
    • Stay in smoke-free places.

When Teachers Push You Out of Your Comfort Zone

Sometimes teachers or mentors try to create new habits in you.

  • They make you do things you do not like.
  • They push you beyond your comfort zone.
  • You may question their purpose (which is okay).
  • Or you may avoid what they ask you to do.

You have two choices:

  • You know more than the teacher (rare, but possible).
  • Or you trust that they are trying to help you grow.

The Choice Is Yours

Old habits feel easy because the path is already made.

To change, you must:

  • Choose the right new path.
  • Walk it many times.
  • Close the old path as much as possible.

In the end, your habits shape your future — and you get to choose which ones stay.

title: Reasons why running might not be for you
content:
Should You Run? How to Know If Running Suits Your Body

Running is a great cardio exercise. You do not need machines – just good shoes and space to move. But running is not the best choice for everyone. Your body type, weight, and fitness level matter.

This guide will help you decide if running is right for you and how to start safely.

Know Your Body Type

When you run, your legs hit the ground with a force about three times your body weight. That is why body type is important.

Experts often talk about three basic body types:

  • Ectomorph: Lean, often tall, finds it hard to gain weight.
  • Endomorph: Bigger build, higher body fat, often stores more fat (pear-shaped).
  • Mesomorph: Muscular, strong, gains muscle easily, has a fast metabolism.

Big Body Types

Some people are “big-built” and may be a mix of two types:

  • Ectomorph + Mesomorph
  • Ectomorph + Endomorph

The ectomorph + mesomorph mix is often great for sprinting:

  • Ectomorph: lighter weight
  • Mesomorph: strong muscles

Small Body Types

People who are short and thin often make good distance runners.

  • Less body weight to move
  • Easier to keep running for long distances
  • Studies show shorter runners can be better at long-distance running than taller runners

Fat Body Types

People with higher body fat (mostly endomorph traits):

  • May get tired more quickly
  • Put more pressure on joints when landing
  • Can still run – but must be more careful and gradual

If You Are Overweight and Want to Run

  • Consult a doctor or expert first.
    Ask about:
    • The right type of shoes
    • The safest running surface
    • How long and how often you should run
  • Start with walking.
    • Begin with slow walks
    • Move to brisk walking
    • Only then start light jogging
  • Watch your heart rate.
    • Extra weight makes running harder on your heart
    • Learn your safe heart rate zone from a doctor
    • Stop if you feel dizzy, breathless, or unwell
  • Rest often.
    • Take breaks in between short running intervals
    • Your body needs time to adapt
    • Rest helps prevent fatigue, injuries, and loss of motivation

Simple Tips to Run Better and Safer

  • Do not eat heavy meals before running.
    • Wait at least 3 hours after a big meal
    • If hungry, eat something light and easy to digest
  • Drink enough water.
    • Drink some water (about half a litre) before your run
    • Do not run when you are very dehydrated
  • Warm up gently.
    • Do light movements and easy stretches
    • Avoid very intense warm-ups if you are a beginner
  • Start slow, then increase speed gradually.
    • Begin at a relaxed pace
    • Speed up slowly as you feel more comfortable
  • Listen to your body.
    • If you feel pain, dizziness, or strong discomfort, stop and rest
    • Start again only when you feel better
  • Know your distance limit.
    • Ask a coach or trainer how much you should run at first
    • Increase distance gradually week by week
  • Choose soft surfaces when possible.
    • Avoid very hard surfaces like concrete roads
    • Run on tracks, grass, or parks to reduce knee impact
  • Cool down and stretch after your run.
    • Walk slowly for a few minutes
    • Stretch your legs, hips, and back
    • This helps prevent cramps and muscle pain

Final Thought

Running is a powerful exercise, but it must match your body and fitness level. Start slow, stay safe, and listen to your body. With the right approach, almost anyone can enjoy running as part of a healthy routine.

title: How To Get Happiness Back In Your Life: 11 Best Questions To Ask Yourself
content:
11 Simple Questions to Bring Happiness Back Into Your Life

Sometimes life gets busy and we forget the good things that are already around us. Asking yourself the right questions can shift your perspective, boost gratitude, and help you feel happier again.

Here are 11 beginner-friendly questions you can ask yourself today.

1. Who am I blessed to have met in my life?

Think of family, friends, teachers, or anyone who helped you grow or inspired you. Feel thankful for their presence.

2. What things do I have right now that make life comfortable?

Look around. Notice simple comforts — your home, your bed, food, internet, clean water, and connection with others.

3. What qualities or skills have I developed over time?

Maybe kindness, humor, listening ability, organization, or self-improvement habits. Celebrate them.

4. What past experiences made me better?

Think of challenges that taught you something — a breakup, a lost job, or a change that led to growth.

5. What things do I enjoy doing?

Books, music, cooking, chatting with friends, hobbies — notice what brings joy into your life.

6. What past desires am I already living today?

Maybe you started saving, learned a skill, took a course, or built confidence. Acknowledge your progress.

7. What unique things do I like about myself?

Maybe your laugh, your memory, your creativity, or your problem-solving ability. Appreciate your uniqueness.

8. What made me smile or laugh today?

A message, a video, a cute moment, good food, or pleasant weather. Notice the tiny joys.

9. What things worked out for me this week?

  • Tasks completed
  • Plans that went smoothly
  • Little wins at home or work

Recognize these successes.

10. How did I help someone this week?

Giving advice, sharing food, helping at home, donating, or simply being kind. Helping others helps us too.

11. What do I appreciate about life in general?

The sunrise, nature, your beating heart, your ability to think, move, love, and learn. Life itself is a gift.

Conclusion

Every small answer adds up. When you focus on what is good, you attract more good into your life.

Make gratitude a habit — the more you look for happiness, the more it grows.

8. Practice Forgiveness

Letting go frees you from stored anger.

  • Keep your heart open
  • Ask: “Can I forgive instead of being angry?”

9. Choose Self-Love First

When you value yourself, anger loses power over you.

  • Be gentle with yourself
  • Ask: “Is this response loving toward me?”

10. Stay Present

When you slow down, you create space to respond wisely.

  • Take conscious breaths before reacting
  • Ask: “Am I grounded in the present moment?”

Small changes in awareness change how you respond. The more you practice these tips, the calmer and happier you become.

title: Essential Guide to Running for Weight Loss
content:
Beginner Guide: How to Build a Running Routine

Running is one of the easiest forms of exercise. You do not need equipment or a gym, and it moves your whole body. A person who weighs around 70 kg can burn about 318 calories in 30 minutes while running. But like any activity, good posture and the right plan help you get better results and avoid injury.

If You Are Starting Out

To lose 1 kg of fat in a week, you need to burn around 3500 calories (around 500 per day). When you begin:

  • Run 3 days a week.
  • Start with 10–15 minutes per session.
  • Add 5 minutes each time until you reach 30–45 minutes.
  • After 4 weeks, increase to 4 running days a week.
  • Once you feel comfortable, start adding short fast intervals or longer distance runs.

If You Are an Intermediate Runner

Once you can run 30–45 minutes comfortably:

  • Add interval training.
  • Run faster than your normal pace for a short time.
  • Example: 3 minutes fast + 2 minutes slow jog for recovery.
  • Intervals help improve speed and help burn more calories.

If You Are in the Advanced Stage

After mastering intervals, you can level up:

  • Add long-distance runs weekly.
  • This improves heart and lung strength.
  • Start strength training—especially your core, hips, and knees.
  • Strong muscles help you run faster and burn fat more efficiently.

Follow these simple stages, increase slowly, and listen to your body for the best results.

title: Best approaches to stop thinking negative thoughts in mind
content:
5 Simple Tips to Overcome Negative Thoughts

Are you tired of negative thinking? These easy tips will help you stay positive and improve your mindset.

1. Have a Positive Attitude Toward Rejection

Rejection hurts, but it is a part of growth. Many successful people failed before winning. For example, the founders of WhatsApp were rejected by Facebook. Instead of giving up, they stayed positive and created their own app. Keep a positive attitude even when things do not go your way.

2. Stop Comparing and Start Living

Comparing yourself to others creates negativity. You may follow someone else’s path even when it does not suit you. Focus on what you love. Live your life based on your interests, not someone else’s achievements.

3. Surround Yourself with Positive People

Your environment affects your mindset. Positive people lift you up with good ideas, stories, and support. Negative people spread fear, doubt, and bad habits. Stay close to people who inspire you and distance yourself from those who drain your energy.

4. Reframe Your Thoughts

Negative thoughts will appear, but you can change how you see them. Instead of treating problems as dead-ends, look at them as redirection. Train your mind to look for options and new ideas. Just like a computer, your brain works better when you remove unhelpful thinking.

5. Keep an Affirmative Approach

A positive attitude helps you stay productive and strong. Successful people change their view of problems so they can find solutions. If people around you spread negativity, protect your mindset and stay away when needed.

Start small, stay consistent, and choose positivity every day.

title: 7 Ways To Attract New Love
content:
7 Simple Ways to Attract New Love Into Your Life

Instead of chasing love, learn how to attract it naturally. Here are easy tips to help you welcome new love into your life.

1. Be Clear About What You Want

Love comes in many forms. Before seeking it, understand what type of relationship you truly need. Ask yourself if you want love for growth, or just to fill a void. Clarity helps you attract the right person.

2. Let Go of Emotional Baggage

Old wounds can block new love. Release past hurts and unhealthy habits. Heal first, so you can enter a new relationship with peace, not pain.

3. Celebrate Others Instead of Being Bitter

Do not compare your life with others. Be happy for people who are in love. When you appreciate love around you, you open space for love within you.

4. Watch Your Self-Talk

Your inner voice matters. If you speak harshly to yourself, stop and change your tone. Talk to yourself with kindness. A positive mind attracts positive love.

5. Surround Yourself With Loving Energy

Fill your space with things that make you happy — books, plants, art, or anything meaningful. When your environment feels loving, your heart does too.

6. Practice Self-Love Daily

You cannot give love if you do not have it within you. Be gentle with yourself, listen to your needs, forgive your mistakes, and appreciate what you have.

7. Be Ready to Receive Love

True love often arrives unexpectedly. When it comes, make sure your heart is open, healed, and prepared to welcome it.

"There is never a time or place for true love. It happens in a heartbeat." – Sarah Dessen

Work on yourself, trust life, and love will find its way to you.

title: Overcoming Doubt
content:
Doubt: The Real Threat to Relationships

Trust is the base of every healthy relationship. When trust breaks, doubt enters. And doubt slowly steals your peace of mind.

Why Does Doubt Appear?

Doubt can come from:

  • Personal insecurity
  • Past emotional wounds
  • Fear of being hurt again
  • Real betrayal from your partner

Sometimes, doubt is not about the partner at all. It can come from childhood neglect, lack of self-worth, or a painful past relationship. Before entering a new relationship, it is important to heal yourself first.

The Dangerous Spiral of Doubt

Doubt creates more questions. Those questions create more doubt. Soon, you feel trapped in a cycle of fear and pain.

When that happens, there are only two choices:

  • Work to remove the doubt
  • Or walk away from the relationship

When Doubt Comes from Betrayal

If your partner has been unfaithful, trust is broken. Many relationships end at this point.

But there is one more powerful ingredient in relationships — hope.

You can choose to forgive if you believe your partner can change and if you believe you can heal.

Relationships Are Built by Imperfect People

Both partners have weaknesses. Both will make mistakes. What matters is:

  • Accepting each other’s flaws
  • Learning from mistakes
  • Ensuring those mistakes are not repeated

Rebuilding Trust Takes Time

Recovering from broken trust is not easy. It needs:

  • Patience
  • Understanding
  • Mutual effort

It is not only the guilty partner’s job. Healing and rebuilding has to be done by both.

Hope Makes Healing Possible

To hope is to believe that trust can grow again — even when there is a reason to doubt.

If both partners are willing to learn, forgive, and try again, the relationship can survive and become even stronger.

title: Secret To Law Of Attraction: 6 Ways How To Get Out Of Your Own Way

6 Ways to Get Out of Your Own Way When Manifesting

The Law of Attraction works best when you stop resisting and start allowing. Sometimes, you block your own desires without knowing it. These simple tips will help you trust more, allow more, and manifest faster.

When you think about the opposite of what you want, you slow down your progress. Shift your attention to joy, appreciation, and what feels good. This clears the path for what you desire.

  • Notice good things around you
  • Appreciate small wins
  • Choose positive thoughts more often

Constantly checking if your desire has arrived creates stress and doubt. Trust that things are already moving. Be gentle with yourself while things unfold.

  • Be patient
  • Believe that the Universe is working for you
  • Support yourself with kindness and self-talk

3. Stay open to new ideas and possibilities

One closed door does not mean failure. The Universe has many ways to deliver what you asked for.

  • Expect new opportunities
  • Look for options you haven’t considered
  • Trust that something better may come

4. Stop forcing and struggling to make things happen

Hard pushing from a negative place creates resistance. Things flow better when you stop forcing outcomes and let go of trying to control everything.

  • Let go of the how, when, and who
  • Stop overthinking the details
  • Allow things to unfold naturally

5. Follow what feels light and inspired

Your emotions are a guidance system. When choices feel heavy, stressful, or forced, wait. When something feels exciting or simple, move toward it.

  • Take inspired action
  • Choose the path of least resistance
  • Listen to your inner feelings

6. Have more fun

Joy speeds things up. When you relax, play, and enjoy life, you naturally align with your desires. Fun brings ideas, synchronicities, and opportunities.

  • Do things that make you smile
  • Be playful and curious
  • Let your happiness lead you

When you stop resisting and start allowing, life starts meeting you halfway. Trust your path, enjoy the process, and watch things fall into place.

title: How To Stay Positive And Easily Manifest Your Desires
content:
10 Simple Ways to Stay Positive in Life

Here are ten easy habits you can practice every day to build a positive atmosphere around you. These simple techniques help raise your energy and make your desires easier to manifest.

#1. Soothe yourself with kind self-talk

When negative situations arise, gently talk to yourself like you would talk to a child. Aim for relief first, then slowly guide your thoughts to something better.

  • Pause
  • Speak kindly to yourself
  • Choose thoughts that feel lighter

#2. Meditate to calm the mind

Meditation helps you release heavy thoughts and return to peace. Even a few minutes of slow breathing can lift your mood and open you to positive ideas.

  • Breathe slowly
  • Count backward from 100
  • Relax your body

#3. Stop staring at the problem

What you focus on grows. If you keep thinking about problems, they expand. Shift attention to something that feels good, so solutions can come more easily.

  • Change the topic in your mind
  • Think of something you enjoy

#4. Leave what drains your energy

Notice how certain people and places make you feel. Choose to spend more time where there is kindness, support, and optimism.

  • Reduce exposure to negativity
  • Seek uplifting environments

#5. Let negative thoughts fade

You don’t have to fight negative thoughts. Simply stop feeding them. If you don’t focus on them, they lose power and disappear naturally.

  • Don’t go deep into bad stories
  • Shift attention instead

#6. Catch negativity early

Notice your thoughts before they grow louder. Ask yourself what you are thinking and whether it is helping you. This makes it easier to release them.

  • Check in with your thoughts
  • Choose thoughts that support you

#7. Become a deliberate thinker

Instead of reacting to everything around you, decide which thoughts you want to keep. You become a creator of your mood, not a reactor to the world.

  • Pick topics that feel good
  • Broadcast the energy you want more of

#8. Practice until positivity becomes stable

With daily practice, positive thinking becomes natural. You will stay steady even when life is messy, because your foundation is strong.

  • Keep practicing good-feeling thoughts
  • Let positivity become your default

#9. Talk about what works

Speak more about what you appreciate, what feels fun, and what brings joy. Positive thoughts attract more positive experiences.

  • Appreciate small wins
  • Share good news

#10. Stop defending or fixing everything

Trying to defend yourself or fix every situation creates stress. Focus on your inner calm first — outer results will adjust on their own.

  • Release the need to prove anything
  • Trust that things are working out

Positivity is a practice. The more you choose it, the easier it becomes — and the better life feels.

title: Choosing yourself
content:
Choosing Yourself Is Not Selfish

Society often teaches us to value others more than ourselves. This is why many people feel confused when choosing between helping others and helping themselves.

Most of the time, we pick others. It feels good to help. It gives us meaning and makes us feel kind and useful.

But sometimes, we go too far.

When Helping Others Hurts You

There are moments when we give even when we have nothing left. We forget our own needs. We push aside our goals, plans, and desires to meet other people’s expectations.

Because of this, the time, money, and energy meant for our growth is handed over to others.

Important Questions to Ask

  • Are we truly fulfilled when we give too much?
  • Or are we just avoiding guilt for saying “no”?
  • Are we really helping others?
  • Or are we encouraging them to depend on us?

Choosing Yourself Matters

Sometimes, the right choice is to choose yourself.

This is not selfish. When you sacrifice your needs all the time, you harm yourself.

Why Self-Care Comes First

  • You deserve time for what you enjoy.
  • You need space to grow and reach your potential.
  • You must stay healthy — mentally, physically, and emotionally.

Only when you are whole, happy, and complete can you truly help others in meaningful ways.

Taking care of yourself first is not selfish — it is the foundation for helping others better.

title: Starting from Scratch: Where to Begin?
content:
Running Basics for Beginners

People have different feelings about running. Some love it, some avoid it. But running is one of the best cardio workouts and gives an energizing “runner’s high”.

If you are a beginner and want to run a marathon, don’t rush. First learn proper running form, then slowly prepare your body.

Running Posture: Do’s and Don’ts

  • Do not land on your heels. Each step creates pressure that travels through your spine. Land on your midfoot or forefoot so your leg muscles absorb the impact.
  • Do not lean forward. Keep your body tall. Imagine a string lifting your chest upward. Avoid hunching to prevent injury.
  • Do not overstride. Your foot should land under your hips. If it lands too far ahead, it wastes energy and increases injury risk.
  • Tuck your elbows in. Avoid swinging your arms across your body. Keep elbows close to save energy.

How to Prepare for Running

Alternate between running days and training days. If you are new, mix jogging and walking:

  • Jog until your heart rate rises.
  • Walk to recover.
  • Repeat for about 20 minutes at first.
  • Increase time as you feel stronger.

Useful Exercises for Runners

  • High knees
  • Butt kicks
  • Power skips
  • Stiff-leg movement
  • Squat jumps
  • Hamstring kick outs (monster walks)

With correct posture and simple training, you will build strength, prevent injuries, and enjoy running more.
